title: Apology at the high school reunion
author: Storytime
hook: At my ten year high school reunion, the girl who ruined my senior year stood up and apologized to me. Then she said who really started it.
story: In senior year, someone spread a rumor that I cheated on the SATs. It wasn't true. But it spread so fast. I lost my spot in the honor society. My college interview got canceled. Everyone believed it was Brittany, the most popular girl in school, because she hated me. I never spoke to her again. Last Saturday was our ten year reunion. I only went because my best friend Kayla begged me. She said, it'll be fun, we'll stick together. Halfway through dinner, Brittany tapped her glass and asked for everyone's attention. She said, I owe someone an apology. She looked right at me. She said, I never started that rumor. But I knew who did, and I said nothing. I've regretted it for ten years. Then she said, the person who started it is sitting right next to you. I turned around. Kayla was staring at her plate. Kayla had wanted my spot in the honor society. She got it. And she got my college interview slot too. Kayla grabbed my hand under the table and whispered, let me explain. Part two?
caption: she said stick together 🙃 #storytime
sound: a slow, tense piano with a dramatic drop at very low volume
why: Rumors and betrayals by old best friends are going viral, Kayla begging her to come is the planted clue, and the whispered let me explain sets up a part two.

title: Sister borrowed my car for a weekend
author: Storytime
hook: My sister borrowed my car for one weekend. It came back with two thousand more miles on it.
story: My little sister Jess asked to borrow my car for the weekend. She said she was helping a friend move across town. Sure, no problem. When she brought it back on Sunday night, I noticed the gas tank was full. Weird. Jess never fills the tank. Then I looked at the odometer. Two thousand and forty miles more than Friday. Across town is ten miles. I asked her where she went. She said, nowhere, just around. So I checked the GPS history. Friday night, she drove eight hundred miles south. To a tiny town I'd never heard of. To an address I didn't recognize. I looked it up. It belongs to a man named Robert Hale. Robert Hale is our father. The father who left when Jess was two, and I was six. The one our mom told us never wanted to see us again. Jess had been writing to him for a year. He's sick. She wanted to meet him before it was too late. She didn't tell me because she knew I'd say no. She came home with a letter. It's addressed to me. I haven't opened it. Should I?
caption: the odometer told me everything 🚗 #storytime
sound: a quiet, emotional road trip guitar at very low volume
why: A small suspicious detail like the odometer is a perfect hook, the full gas tank is a clever planted clue, and the unopened letter question drives a lot of emotional comments.

title: Kid stealing packages from my porch
author: Storytime
hook: Someone kept stealing parcels from my porch. My doorbell camera showed my eight year old neighbour.
story: For three weeks, my parcels kept disappearing. A phone case. Some books. A coffee machine. The delivery app said delivered every time. So I checked my doorbell camera. Every afternoon, about ten minutes after the van left, a small boy in a dinosaur jumper ran up, grabbed the parcel, and ran next door. It was Leo. Eight years old. His mum is a nurse who works long shifts. I didn't want to call the police on a child. So I knocked on their door. Leo opened it, saw me, and his face lit up. He said, wait here. He came back with a notebook and took me to the garden shed. Inside were all my parcels. Stacked neatly. Each one with a sticky note. Mr. Parker, kept safe, Tuesday. He showed me his notebook. He'd written down the number plate of a silver car that kept stopping at houses on our street, right after deliveries. He'd been protecting my parcels from the real thief. I sent the number plate to the police. They arrested a man that same week, with a garage full of stolen parcels. Leo wants a reward. What should I get him?
caption: he wasn't the thief. he was security 🦖 #storytime
sound: a playful, sneaky detective beat at very low volume
why: Package theft rises before Black Friday, the doorbell footage hook makes people assume the worst, the kid hero twist is shareable, and the reward question pulls lots of comments.
